question: Can women perform i'tikaf at home?
answer:
So out of the four schools of law, the Hanafi, Hanbali, Shafi'i and Maliki, only the Hanafis allow i'tikaf in houses for the women. The other three madhhabs do not allow i'tikaf in places other than masajid. And Allah 'azza wa jall says in the Qur'an, "And do not come close to your spouses when you are doing i'tikaf in the masajid." And that is why the other three madhhabs say there is no concept of i'tikaf in the house. And I must say that that is the position that I follow as well: **there is no i'tikaf in the house.**

Now, that is my opinion. Our Hanafi brethren would disagree, and they have every right to disagree. And you know my position about the madhhabs: we respect, and we respectfully agree and disagree. And so if you ask me, my position is that there is no i'tikaf in the house. If you ask any respected Hanafi, Deobandi 'alim, they will say that it is allowed to do i'tikaf inside the house, and they will give you the conditions and the rulings for that.

Nonetheless, even if I tell you there is no i'tikaf in the house, and this is the position of the majority of scholars, still that does not mean that you cannot do extra worship in your house, that you cannot have a corner and a time in a place where you go into a bubble, and everybody knows you are now not to be disturbed. And you tell your husband and your children, "From this time to this time, I want to just worship Allah," and they all, alhamdulillah, give you that time and space. Why not? I wouldn't call it i'tikaf, me personally; that's not my position. I will say this is your time of worship of Allah. Why can't you do that?

So you ask me, and I say there is no i'tikaf in the house. There's no concept of i'tikaf inside the house. None of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ ever did i'tikaf inside the house. Even they would do i'tikaf privately in the masjid; they would have corners of the masjid, and they would do it over there. However, that does not negate the fact that you can assign a time and a place that you feel logistically, not for any act of worship, logistically: let's just say, from 4pm to 5pm, everybody knows, "I'm reading Qur'an in this corner; nobody should disturb me." Okay, fine. Make that a rule. And it's a logistic rule that everybody knows; it's just convenient for you to do that. And that would be something great that you should do in this Ramadan, and in fact throughout the year if possible.
